name: Kuro and Walking Route
description: Kuro is living in a country called Uberland, consisting of $$$n$$$ towns, numbered from $$$1$$$ to $$$n$$$, and $$$n - 1$$$ bidirectional roads connecting these towns. It is possible to reach each town from any other. Each road connects two towns $$$a$$$ and $$$b$$$. Kuro loves walking and he is planning to take a walking marathon, in which he will choose a pair of towns $$$(u, v)$$$ ($$$u \neq v$$$) and walk from $$$u$$$ using the shortest path to $$$v$$$ (note that $$$(u, v)$$$ is considered to be different from $$$(v, u)$$$). Oddly, there are 2 special towns in Uberland named Flowrisa (denoted with the index $$$x$$$) and Beetopia (denoted with the index $$$y$$$). Flowrisa is a town where there are many strong-scent flowers, and Beetopia is another town where many bees live. In particular, Kuro will avoid any pair of towns $$$(u, v)$$$ if on the path from $$$u$$$ to $$$v$$$, he reaches Beetopia after he reached Flowrisa, since the bees will be attracted with the flower smell on Kuro’s body and sting him. Kuro wants to know how many pair of city $$$(u, v)$$$ he can take as his route. Since he’s not really bright, he asked you to help him with this problem.
input_specification: The first line contains three integers $$$n$$$, $$$x$$$ and $$$y$$$ ($$$1 \leq n \leq 3 \cdot 10^5$$$, $$$1 \leq x, y \leq n$$$, $$$x \ne y$$$) - the number of towns, index of the town Flowrisa and index of the town Beetopia, respectively. $$$n - 1$$$ lines follow, each line contains two integers $$$a$$$ and $$$b$$$ ($$$1 \leq a, b \leq n$$$, $$$a \ne b$$$), describes a road connecting two towns $$$a$$$ and $$$b$$$. It is guaranteed that from each town, we can reach every other town in the city using the given roads. That is, the given map of towns and roads is a tree.
output_specification: A single integer resembles the number of pair of towns $$$(u, v)$$$ that Kuro can use as his walking route.
approach_summary: Precompute 2^k ancestor jumps up[u][k] and node depths in O(N log N). Compute LCA and path aggregates in O(log N) per query.

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 979C — Kuro and Walking Route [146. Binary Lifting and LCA]
topic_editorial.summary: Binary lifting for lowest common ancestor and tree jumps.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: Any ancestor jump of distance $K$ can be decomposed into powers of two $K = \sum 2^j$. Precomputing `up[u][k]` (the $2^k$-th ancestor of $u$) via `up[u][k] = up[up[u][k-1]][k-1]` allows any path or LCA to be answered in $O(\log N)$.
